title: A generative, compressed genome pushes evolution toward general-purpose problem solvers

fields.label: Label
fields.value: A generative, compressed genome pushes evolution toward general-purpose problem solvers

fields.label: Statement
fields.value: By using an architecture akin to a variational autoencoder, in which the genome is a compressed generative representation decoded by the developmental layer, evolution is kept from over-training on past conditions and is pushed to produce general-purpose problem-solving organisms that display robustness, plasticity and adaptive success in entirely novel circumstances.

fields.label: Work
fields.value: Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology

fields.label: Chapter
fields.value: Levin M 2023, Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology › Intelligence and evolution: the impact of competency at new scales

fields.label: Quotation
fields.value: Second is that by using a variational autoencoder-like architecture of compression into a generative genome (Fig. 1), evolution is freed from over-training on past conditions and pushed to evolve general-purpose problem-solving machines which inevitably display robustness, plasticity, and adaptive success in entirely novel circumstances.

fields.label: Assumptions
fields.value: Levin M, “Darwin's agential materials: evolutionary implications of multiscale competency in developmental biology”, Cellular and molecular life sciences : CMLS (2023), doi:10.1007/s00018-023-04790-z; section “Intelligence and evolution: the impact of competency at new scales”. Scope: Evolution of multicellular organisms

fields.label: Assessment
fields.value: GPT-5.6 Sol on levin-2023-agential-03: partially-resolvable, resolvability 0.53

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: A strong restricted version can be tested with evolutionary computation using standard methods. Existing public biological datasets do not directly encode architecture, training history, and novel-condition performance across the broad scope.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Evolve matched direct and compressed generative genotype-to-phenotype architectures on training environments, then measure performance and plasticity on held-out novel perturbations. Better out-of-distribution performance for compressed architectures across controls would support the mechanism.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Novelty and general-purpose success require chosen benchmarks.

The genome-to-VAE analogy is not a literal specified architecture.

Simulation results may not generalize to organisms.

fields.label: Dimension scores
fields.value:
operationalizability: 0.62
data adequacy: 0.35
data existence: 0.5
analysis feasibility: 0.58
discriminating power: 0.62

fields.label: Finding
fields.value: Indirect encodings in the two public models can be scored for performance off the training conditions, which tests a narrow version of the architectural claim. Neither model is a variational autoencoder of a metazoan genome, and success in those runs would not show that evolution is freed from over-training or that plasticity in organisms is produced by that compression.

fields.label: Proposed test in the assessment
fields.value: Proposed test with existing data: Compare public evolutionary runs that use a compressed generative encoding with otherwise matched direct encodings, and score robustness and success on environments not seen during selection. Higher novel-environment success for the generative encoding would support the architectural prediction; no difference, or a difference explained by parameter count alone, would count against it.

fields.label: Evidence against
fields.value:
Robustness in a toy embryogeny does not show that real evolution is pushed to general-purpose problem solvers.

The autoencoder analogy is not a unique encoding, so several implementations can be called confirmatory.
